events.body:
The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so extra kilometres enter the fare [F7]; the excess-distance billing of $11.96 on 8.5 km confirms the per-km rate of $1.41 [F5], consistent with distance_fare $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.4075 ≈ $1.41/km [F7][RD-2].

Two off-route segments exist: F3 (18:40–18:45, +3.17 km) and F4 (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) [F3][F4][RD-1]. Each is reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1].

Segment F3: the driver asked at 18:37 whether he could "go round via Kranji Expressway" and the rider replied at 18:38 "Sure, go ahead" [F8][F9][F10]. That is a rider message sent before the 18:40:50 segment start agreeing to a road the driver named; the exchange ties itself to the next off-route segment, and nothing in the record shows a different destination [F8][F9][RD-5]. The segment is therefore exempt in full [RD-5].

Segment F4: the detour began 18:59, more than 20 minutes after the only rider agreement, with no further rider message anywhere in the complete, fully timestamped two-message chat [F9][F10]; the driver's post-trip statement that the "second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is not rider consent (G11) [F11][RD-5]. RD-4 relief fails — no qualifying incident, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. No rider-named stop is measured in this segment [F3][F4][RD-3]. The segment counts as a non-exempt deviation and the extra km are refundable [RD-2].

Amount: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74 [F4][F5][F7][RD-2]. F3's 3.17 km is exempt and is not counted; the residual map-matching difference against the $11.96 excess is not refunded [F5][RD-2]. Total refund $6.74, issued as a voucher, Ryde retaining final discretion [RD-2][NS-7].

Account action: the driver's profile shows 1 dispute upheld in 90 days, but 0 route disputes upheld [F17], so the "repeated route breach" condition of RD-6 is not met and no flag is raised [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement [F8][F9][F11] plus the route facts [F3][F4][F14][F15]; no threats, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appear — the complaint is purely about the fare [RD-1? no — SAFE-1]. Nothing requires escalation.

We're sending you a Ryde voucher for $6.74. Nothing changes on your account. Thanks for flagging it.

A second detour later in the trip was not agreed to, so 4.78 extra kilometres were refunded to the rider: $6.74, paid as a Ryde voucher. No flag has been placed on your account, and no other action is being taken. Keep in mind that future detours need the rider's agreement in chat, since GPS rerouting alone isn't consent.

The trip is RydeTAXI (metered), so extra kilometres enter the fare [F7]; the excess-distance billing of $11.96 on 8.5 km confirms the per-km rate of $1.41 [F5], consistent with distance_fare $40.96 ÷ 29.1 km = $1.4075 ≈ $1.41/km [F7][RD-2].

Two off-route segments exist: F3 (18:40–18:45, +3.17 km) and F4 (18:59–19:08, +4.78 km) [F3][F4][RD-1]. Each is reviewed separately under RD-3/RD-4/RD-5 [RD-1].

Segment F3: the driver asked at 18:37 whether he could "go round via Kranji Expressway" and the rider replied at 18:38 "Sure, go ahead" [F8][F9][F10]. That is a rider message sent before the 18:40:50 segment start agreeing to a road the driver named; the exchange ties itself to the next off-route segment, and nothing in the record shows a different destination [F8][F9][RD-5]. The segment is therefore exempt in full [RD-5].

Segment F4: the detour began 18:59, more than 20 minutes after the only rider agreement, with no further rider message anywhere in the complete, fully timestamped two-message chat [F9][F10]; the driver's post-trip statement that the "second turn-off was my GPS rerouting" is not rider consent (G11) [F11][RD-5]. RD-4 relief fails — no qualifying incident, and a speed band alone does not exempt [F12][F13][F14][RD-4]. No rider-named stop is measured in this segment [F3][F4][RD-3]. The segment counts as a non-exempt deviation and the extra km are refundable [RD-2].

Amount: 4.78 km × $1.41/km = $6.74 [F4][F5][F7][RD-2]. F3's 3.17 km is exempt and is not counted; the residual map-matching difference against the $11.96 excess is not refunded [F5][RD-2]. Total refund $6.74, issued as a voucher, Ryde retaining final discretion [RD-2][NS-7].

Account action: the driver's profile shows 1 dispute upheld in 90 days, but 0 route disputes upheld [F17], so the "repeated route breach" condition of RD-6 is not met and no flag is raised [F17][RD-6].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement [F8][F9][F11] plus the route facts [F3][F4][F14][F15]; no threats, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation appear — the complaint is purely about the fare [RD-1? no — SAFE-1]. Nothing requires escalation.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider advocate requested no_action, but F4 is a non-exempt off-route segment of 4.78 km with no rider agreement in the complete chat [F10][F11][RD-5] and no traffic incident [F14][RD-4], so $6.74 is refundable under RD-2.

If read as the driver's request for no_action across both segments: the consent in F9 covers the Kranji exchange (F3) only, not the later 18:59 detour, which he himself calls GPS rerouting [F11]; F4 therefore fails RD-5 and counts [RD-2], and his post-trip statement of agreement cannot substitute for rider consent (G11).

segment_findings.reason: Driver named the Kranji Expressway detour at 18:37 and the rider agreed at 18:38, both before the segment start (18:40); the named alternative road ties to this next off-route segment and the complete chat shows no different destination — exempt under RD-5.

The only rider agreement (18:38) precedes this 18:59 second detour, which the driver himself attributes to GPS rerouting; the complete timestamped chat (F10) contains no rider consent to this segment and his statement is not consent (G11). RD-4 fails (no incident) and RD-3 has no rider-named stop here — refundable under RD-2.

notices.text: Good news — we've refunded part of your RydeTAXI fare. Your trip had two detours. The first one you agreed to in chat, so it doesn't count. The second detour, which started about 20 minutes later, was not agreed to, so you were charged for 4.78 extra kilometres. At $1.41 per kilometre, that comes to $6.74. We're sending you a Ryde voucher for $6.74. Nothing changes on your account. Thanks for flagging it.

We reviewed the fare dispute on your RydeTAXI trip. One detour was agreed to by the rider in the app chat, so it doesn't count against you. A second detour later in the trip was not agreed to, so 4.78 extra kilometres were refunded to the rider: $6.74, paid as a Ryde voucher. No flag has been placed on your account, and no other action is being taken. Keep in mind that future detours need the rider's agreement in chat, since GPS rerouting alone isn't consent.
